x: The usual cold, misty weather greeted the starters for this year's race, but soon warming to his task, Jack Brown set about the opposition in no uncertain manner and was soon in the leading bunch with Salvat of Finchley and Cameron of T.V.H.

Just right for Charlie who likes opposition such as this and he really rose to the occasion, and despite an early set-back when Cameron(T.V.H.), running very strongly, passed and went away, he made progress to such an extent as to take us up to 7th and at the same time produced a Belgrave best for the stage.

It was on this leg that tragedy struck T.V.H.; Cameron collapsing with an injury when in 2nd place a mile from the take over. Ken Miller, dogged by injury during the previous few months had come into the team only during the previous few days, when Malcolm Robinson was forced to withdraw.

Arthur Thomson of Metropolitan led from start to finish and beat his team mate Don Thompson by nearly 2 mins. in 76:54. Our first man home was Bob Barnes (9th in 84:01) followed by Cameron (19th in 89 22 and Fotheringham (21st in 93:19).

John Knifton was 24th in Section A Barnes, Belderson, Beecham and Keown, 6th 7th 30th and 32nd respectively in Section B; Eglington, Cameron, McLennan, Duncan,Wilson and Doubleday between 18 and 62 in Section C; Bushman, East and Logan 14th,15th and 34th in Section D.
In the'Middlesex' at Regents Park, our Cadogan A.C. team finished 5th. Cameron, Checkley & L. Jones finishing 16th, 18th and 19th respectively.
Ray Hall was 10th (56:19), Jones 18th (58:50), Cameron 22nd (60:05), Keown 28th (61:12). Other members also took part in the match held in conjunction.

Even the loss of King, Barnes and Cameron during the race did not affect the result. In the individual race Ray Middleton walked exceptionally well and coming thro' in his usual style was only 43 seconds short of catching the winner, Nihill.
Dave King came through well followed by Pat Duncan. Without Farley, Baker, Cameron or Picton it was left to John Keown to bring the team in fourth.

A good Belgrave turnout for the first of the '7's saw Len Duquemin take first place and lead the team in first as well. Cameron and Wesch walked well but were edged out by Carl Lawton as fourth scorer.
